exercises.prompt: Match each stage to the role it plays, from material through truth.

feedback.note: The senses supply material in the form of percepts. Reason identifies and integrates that material. Truth is the recognition of reality, and reason is its standard.

feedback.quote: Reason is the faculty that identifies and integrates the material provided by man's senses.
feedback.note: The last word is senses. Substituting feelings would make reason a rationalizer of emotion, which the interview denies.
feedback.citation: Ayn Rand, "The Objectivist Ethics," The Virtue of Selfishness, 20

exercises.prompt: What does this unit mean by truth?

choices.text: The recognition of reality, with reason as the only standard
A feeling that reality has matched a wish
Whatever a group agrees to call real
A name detached from any recognition of the facts

feedback.quote: Truth is the recognition of reality; reason, man's only means of knowledge, is his only standard of truth.
feedback.note: Truth is tied to reality, and the standard named in the sentence is reason, not feeling and not a vote.
feedback.citation: Ayn Rand, Galt's Speech, For the New Intellectual, 126

exercises.prompt: “Reason is man’s only means of grasping reality and of acquiring knowledge” implies which consequence, in the same sentence?

feedback.quote: Reason is man's only means of grasping reality and of acquiring knowledge—and, therefore, the rejection of reason means that men should act regardless of and/or in contradiction to the facts of reality.
feedback.note: The “therefore” is part of the sentence. It is a consequence she draws, not a separate slogan.
feedback.citation: Ayn Rand, "The Left: Old and New," Return of the Primitive: The Anti-Industrial Revolution, 162

choices.text: Rejecting reason means acting regardless of, or against, the facts

Society becomes the means of knowledge

exercises.prompt: A philosophic system, in the West Point lecture, is:

feedback.quote: A philosophic system is an integrated view of existence.
feedback.note: The sentence defines a philosophic system as one view, not a pile of tips. This floor only asks for that definition.
feedback.citation: Ayn Rand, "Philosophy: Who Needs It," Philosophy: Who Needs It, 5

feedback.quote: The arguments of those who attack the senses are merely variants of the fallacy of the "stolen concept."
feedback.note: You can now say what is stolen: the evidential base the argument still stands on.
